rationales: Species is the narrowest taxonomic rank listed, not the broadest.
Genus is broader than species but narrower than kingdom and domain.
Kingdom is broad, but domain is a broader rank.
Domain is the broadest taxonomic rank listed.
Archaea lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls, unlike bacteria.
Archaea are prokaryotes and therefore do not have a nucleus.
Many archaea are known for living in extreme environments, making this the best choice among the options.
Archaea have ribosomes, as do all cellular organisms.
Bacteria do not have a nucleus.
Many bacteria have cell walls containing peptidoglycan.
Many bacteria are heterotrophic, although some are autotrophic.
Bacteria do not have chloroplasts; some can photosynthesize using structures that are not chloroplasts.
Escherichia coli is a bacterium in the domain Bacteria, not Eukarya.
Yeast is a eukaryotic organism and belongs to the domain Eukarya.
Coronavirus is a virus, not a cellular organism classified in domain Eukarya.
Yeast belongs to Eukarya, so this option is incorrect.
Some eukaryotic cells have cell walls, so their defining distinction is not a lack of cell walls.
Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus, whereas prokaryotic cells do not.
Both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells contain ribosomes.
Eukaryotic cells are generally larger than prokaryotic cells, so smaller size is not their distinguishing feature.
Archaea are prokaryotic, not eukaryotic.
Protists are eukaryotic and are often unicellular and heterotrophic.
Fungi are eukaryotic and heterotrophic, but most are multicellular rather than primarily unicellular.
Plants are eukaryotic but are generally multicellular and autotrophic.
Chitin in the cell wall is a fungal characteristic, but it does not explain why fungi are heterotrophs.
Fungi obtain food by absorbing nutrients from their surroundings, which is a heterotrophic mode of nutrition.
Reproduction by spores does not determine whether an organism is heterotrophic.
Fungi cannot make their own food, which is true, but absorbing nutrients describes how they obtain it.
Viruses are acellular and lack organelles, so they do not fit the traditional kingdoms of cellular life.
Many cellular organisms also cannot photosynthesize, so this does not explain why viruses are excluded from kingdoms.
Small size does not prevent an organism from being classified in a kingdom.
Being parasitic does not prevent cellular organisms from being classified in kingdoms.
Homo sapiens is correctly written with the genus capitalized and the species epithet lowercase; scientific names are conventionally italicized.

The genus name should begin with a capital letter, so homo sapiens is incorrectly capitalized.

A scientific name does not directly provide both phylum and genus.
